messages.author: 5657e1d4422ecd3a
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#491] Problems with negative keys
parts:
You have to use the sum function instead of length in the reduce function.  Also, it is best to provide combine=T argument to mapreduce.  Here is the revised code with the rmr2 package:

require(rmr2)
t <- read.table("http://dl.dropbox.com/u/6960256/data/centralparktemps.txt", header=T,quote="\"")

hdfs.temp <- to.dfs(temp)
out = mapreduce(
  input = hdfs.temp,

map = function(k,v) keyval(round((v-32)*5/9,0), 1),
  reduce = function(k,vv) keyval(k, sum(vv)),
  combine=T)
df = as.data.frame( from.dfs(out))

messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#501] Problems with negative keys
parts:
You will have to use the input.format argument to mapreduce.  The values are passed to mapreduce as data.frames.  The links to the documentation below will give you some idea how to specify a CSV format.  Note that the header=T argument to read.table is not honored. If you want column names, you should specify header=F and use the colnames argument for read.table. 
  • https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RHadoop/wiki/rmr-v1.2-Overview - Note that there are differences between rmr1.2 and rmr2.
  • https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RHadoop/wiki/Getting-data-in-and-out

messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#502] Problems with negative keys
parts:
If your data is in CSV you should use the csv format. header = F is
already set because the way hadoop works it's hard to have access to
the headers whenever needed (if a CSV file is partitioned, what happen
to the headers?). I am not saying it's unsolvable, just not trivial,
there is an open issue about it. As Jayanth says, you have to specify
the col names when defining the input format. Then you just get a data
frame as the value argument in the map function with the right column
names. But if the data was created in R and loaded into HDFS with
to.dfs, as in your example, it should still work. This is what happens
when I try it.

temp = read.table("http://dl.dropbox.com/u/6960256/data/centralparktemps.txt",
header=T,quote="\"")
str(from.dfs(mapreduce(to.dfs(temp), map = function(k,v) v$temperature)))

List of 2
$ key: NULL
$ val: num [1:1716] 35.1 37.5 28.3 28.8 28.6 34.2 23.8 36.6 27.7 30.3 ...


Antonio
